metrics.name: Visual Clarity
metrics.description: Measures whether text is legible and whether contrast, type, spacing, alignment, color, and density make the screen's structure and priorities clear at a glance.
metrics.weight_rationale: Equals the sum of its ten members' current weights (23), kept unchanged because contrast and hierarchy still dominate the group and no member overlaps with another group.

metrics.name: Interaction and Feedback
metrics.description: Measures whether users can tell what is operable, see what the system is doing, avoid mistakes, and recover or back out when something goes wrong.
metrics.weight_rationale: Equals the sum of its nine members' current weights (29), the largest group because it holds both error metrics (5 each) and the action-to-outcome loop that decides task success.

metrics.name: Accessibility
metrics.description: Measures whether keyboard, screen reader, and imprecise-pointer users can reach, identify, and operate every control.
metrics.weight_rationale: Equals the sum of its four members' current weights (16), kept as a separate group so that blocking access failures are not averaged away inside a larger one.

metrics.name: Content and Cognitive Effort
metrics.description: Measures whether users can find what they need, understand labels, icons, and messages, and finish tasks without extra steps or reliance on memory.
metrics.weight_rationale: Equals the sum of its eight members' current weights (20), led by navigation and information architecture at 4 each.

metrics.name: Consistency and Context Fit
metrics.description: Measures whether the screen behaves like one coherent, trustworthy product that matches its platform and holds up across widths, themes, and languages.
metrics.weight_rationale: Equals the sum of its six members' current weights (12), the smallest group because most of its checks concern conditions beyond the single screen being scored.
